description.narrative: Den begränsade insatsen avser genomförandet av en slutlig fas av kapacitetsstöd i form av rådgivning genom konsultfirman Adam Smith International (ASI) till den irakiska premiärministerns kansli (PMO) i dess ansträngningar att etablera en resultatenhet (RU) inom kansliet med uppgift att följa upp ministeriernas bidrag till genomförandet av det strategiska regeringsprogrammet. Syftet är att stärka möjligheten för premiärministern att hålla ministrar och ministerier ansvariga för sina bidrag till regeringsprogrammet, för premiärministern att kunna ta välinformerade prioriteringsbeslut i förhållande till regeringsprogrammet samt kunna redovisa regerinsprogrammets genomförande till parlamentet och medborgarna. Därutöver har en komponent för kapacitetsstöd tillkommit som avser rådgivning kring PMOs roll i de olika kriskommittéer som inrättas på central nivå med uppgift att samordna stöd insatser i områden som fritas från ISIS, inklusive återvänande för internflyktingar, i nära dialog med det internationella givarsamfundet. Syftet med kapacitetsstödet är att stärka PMOs ledarroll i kommittéerna.

TSI contributes to increased democratic governance at central level and enables such developments at local level. TSI is a consultant implemented project in support for the Council of Ministers Secretariat in its technocratic role supporting the government of Iraq in terms of central policy and budget planning and follow up.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2016Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: Sida supported Technical Support to Iraq phase 3 (TSI 3) between 2012 and 2016. The intervention was in the form of a technical assistance consultancy with the areas and scope of work agreed upon between Sida and the Government of Iraq (GoI), based on GoI's priorities. Adam Smith International (which had also carried out previous phases of technical assistance to the Iraqi government institutions) was procured by Sida for the assignment. Due to the serious security situation in Iraq, a separate agreement was made between Sida and the UK FCO for the FCO to provide the consultants with security arrangements, room, board and office space at their premises within the Green Zone in Baghdad (where the government institutions are also located). In total (ASI consultancy, FCO arrangement + monitoring), Sida contributed SEK 94 828 124 to TSI 3.
During the extension period of TSI 3, 2015 - 2016, a Results Unit was set up with the task of providing the Iraqi Prime Minister (PM) with quality and verified reports on the progress on his strategic priorities and options on how to resolve issues hindering the achievement of results in order to improve the quality of decision making, as well as ensuring that the principle of delivering results and being accountable for these results is implemented within the government.
After significant delays on this output, the Results Unit was established in the Council of Ministers Secretariat (CoMSec) instead of in the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) as originally planned. TSI provided support in adjusting the design and core processes of the Results Unit to its position in CoMSec, training assigned CoMSec staff and clarifying the roles and responsibilities of the Results Unit and the linkages of various directorates in CoMSec to avoid duplication of work.
Also, through support provided by TSI, the PMO (with inputs from CoMSec) prepared the first annual progress report on the strategic priorities of the government, including an update on the implementation of the political agreement that underpins the governing coalition, in December 2015. The report and its roll-out plan to the Council of Representatives (Iraq's parliament) and the general public was approved by the PM. The progress report was being updated for the release of the second annual report at the time of the closure of TSI in August 2016.
Moreover, TSI supported the GoI in improving its crisis management structure so that it could better support stabilization in areas retaken from Daesh. This resulted in the structure being rationalized after TSI presented an overview of the various bodies handling and reporting on different and occasionally overlapping aspects of crisis management. The reports prepared by the crisis committee were altered after TSI advised that crisis management developments should be more clearly presented to the PM and CoM. The crisis committee also adopted a work planning and information comparison approach at the advice of TSI. The PMO Chief of Staff stated that he noticed significantly improved support by the crisis management committee.
